requirements: Students shall be able to view the courses being offered and the number of seats still available in each course.
Students shall be able to view course details including the course title, instructor, class time, capacity, and remaining seats.
Students shall be able to register for a course that has a seat available.
The system shall tell a student whether a registration succeeded and shall give a reason when it did not succeed.
The system shall not register the same student for the same course more than once.
The system shall not accept registrations beyond the capacity of a course.
Students shall be able to view the courses for which they are registered.
Students shall be able to cancel their own registration during the registration period.
When a registration is cancelled, the corresponding seat shall become available again.
If several students attempt to take the last available seat at the same time, the system shall not exceed the course capacity.
If one student submits several registration attempts for the same course at the same time, the system shall retain only one registration.
Course and registration information shall not be lost when the application or its server is restarted.
The application shall be deployable as a container running on Linux virtual machines.
Authoritative course registration state shall not be kept only in the local storage of one application instance, so that a replacement instance can process subsequent requests.
The system that stores course registration information shall not be directly accessible from the Internet.
Environment-specific configuration and secrets shall be supplied when the service is run rather than included in the application artifact.
The operating environment shall be able to determine automatically whether an application instance is ready to process requests.
The cloud environment required by the service shall be reproducibly created and removed from a version-controlled infrastructure definition.
For the initial pilot, a temporary service interruption caused by an application server failure is acceptable.
cloudConstraints: The university will pilot the service in the AWS Seoul Region (ap-northeast-2), and the monthly cloud budget must not exceed 500 USD. The fixed research scope is Docker on Linux virtual machines with Terraform and temporary HTTP endpoints. HTTPS, TLS certificates, and domain management are outside this pilot. The pilot may not use a managed database service, Kubernetes, or serverless compute and must use synthetic data instead of real personal data. Recovery from a data-storage server failure is outside this pilot.
